Package index

Alpha Diversity

Calculate within-sample diversity using various indices.

alpha_div()
Alpha Diversity Wrapper Function

Richness metrics

Estimators focused on the number of species (richness).

ace()
Abundance-based Coverage Estimator (ACE)
chao1()
Chao1 Richness Estimator
margalef()
Margalef's Richness Index
menhinick()
Menhinick's Richness Index
observed()
Observed Features
squares()
Squares Richness Estimator

Coverage metrics

Estimates of how completely a sample covers its community.

Phylogenetic metrics

Diversity based on phylogenetic branch lengths.

faith()
Faith's Phylogenetic Diversity (PD)

Depth and coverage

Diversity against sequencing depth and sample coverage. Rarefaction and extrapolation of Hill numbers (iNEXT), and every sample’s Hill numbers at one common depth or coverage, to compare or test.

hill_extrapolation() hill_standardize()

plot(<ecodive_hill_extrapolation>)
Plot interpolated and extrapolated Hill numbers
rarefaction_curve()
Rarefaction Curves

Compositional Data

Log ratios for relative abundances. The centered log ratios (clr and rclr) are norm choices; see normalize().

Zeros

Replace zeros before taking log ratios, instead of adding a pseudocount. replace_zeros() runs any method by name.

replace_zeros()
Zero Replacement
replace_zeros_mult()
Multiplicative Zero Replacement
replace_zeros_gbm() replace_zeros_sq() replace_zeros_bl() replace_zeros_czm()
Bayesian-Multiplicative and Count Zero Replacement
list_zero_replacements() match_zero_replacement()
Find and Browse Zero Replacement Methods

Log-ratio transforms

Coordinates for analyses of the transformed features themselves. For distances, use aitchison().

alr()
Additive Log-Ratio Transform
ilr()
Isometric Log-Ratio Transform
philr()
Phylogenetic Isometric Log-Ratio Transform (PhILR)

Log ratios

One log ratio per sample, between two groups of features, to use as a variable in tests and models.

log_ratio()
Log Ratio of Summed Abundances
balance()
Isometric Log-Ratio Balance
log_ratio_features()
Features for a Log Ratio from a Ranking

Proportionality

Which features keep a constant ratio across samples, the compositionally valid alternative to correlation. A dist over the features.

vlr()
Variance of Log Ratios
rho_p()
Proportionality Correlation
phi_s()
Symmetric Proportionality

Diagnostics

First looks at a composition before analysing it. variation_array() summarizes every pair of features’ log ratios and each feature’s share of the total variance; zero_pattern() shows which features are zero together, before choosing a pseudocount or replace_zeros() method.

variation_array()
Variation Array
zero_pattern()
Zero Patterns

Associations and networks

Correlations between features’ absolute abundances, estimated from relative abundances (a dist over the features), the pairs above a cutoff, and the networks they make. feature_assoc() runs any association measure by name.

sparcc()
SparCC Correlation
feature_assoc()
Associations Between Features
list_feature_assocs() match_feature_assoc()
Find and Browse Association Measures
assoc_pairs()
Strongly Associated Pairs of Features
assoc_network()
Association Network
assoc_network_compare()
Compare Two Association Networks
assoc_network_diff()
Differential Associations

Associations between tables

Correlations between the features of one table (taxa) and the variables of another measured on the same samples (environmental factors, metabolites), with adjusted p-values and a starred heatmap.

cross_assoc()
Associations Between Two Tables
plot(<ecodive_cross_assoc>)
Plot Associations Between Two Tables

Differential abundance

Which features’ abundances differ between groups. da_test() runs any method by name; the classical per-feature tests compare normalized values, the others log ratios or clr values, so that the samples’ totals don’t matter.

da_test()
Differential Abundance Testing
list_da_tests() match_da_test()
Find and Browse Differential Abundance Methods
da_sensitivity()
Sensitivity of a Differential Abundance Analysis
ancom()
Analysis of Composition of Microbiomes (ANCOM)
ancombc() ancombc2()
Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction (ANCOM-BC)
ancombc_global() ancombc_pairwise() ancombc_dunnett() ancombc_trend()
Post-hoc tests for ANCOM-BC and ANCOM-BC2
structural_zeros()
Structural zeros
fastancom()
ANCOM from Marginal Models (fastANCOM)
dirmult_ttest()
Dirichlet-multinomial Welch t-tests (ALDEx2-style)
dirmult_lm()
Dirichlet-multinomial linear models with scale models (ALDEx3)
da_wilcoxon() da_ttest() da_lm()
Per-feature Wilcoxon, t and Linear Model Tests
linda()
Linear Models for Differential Abundance (LinDA)
maaslin3()
Multivariable Association with Linear Models (MaAsLin 3)
lefse()
LEfSe: LDA Effect Size Biomarker Discovery
indicator_species()
Indicator Species Analysis

Absolute abundance

With each sample’s total microbial load measured (cell counts, qPCR, a spike-in), estimate absolute abundances instead of ratios.

qmp_scale() qmp_rarefy()
Quantitative Microbiome Profiling: Absolute Abundances from a Measured Load

Community types

Assign each sample to one of a few community types. The types come back as a data frame whose type column can be used as groups in any test or ordination plot.

enterotype()
Enterotypes
valencia()
VALENCIA community state types
valencia_centroids
VALENCIA's reference centroids
dmm()
Dirichlet-multinomial mixtures
ecodive_types
Community types

Source Tracking

What share of each sink sample’s community came from each of several source environments, and from an unknown source.

sourcetracker()
Microbial source tracking (SourceTracker)

Quality Control

Find the features that come from contaminating DNA, by their frequency against each sample’s DNA concentration and their prevalence in negative controls (decontam).

decontam() decontam_not()
Contaminant Identification (decontam)
plot(<ecodive_decontam>) plot(<ecodive_decontam_not>)
Plot decontam() results
decontam_frequency_plot()
Plot Feature Frequency against DNA Concentration (decontam)

Community Assembly

How far drift and dispersal alone explain a community’s composition (Sloan’s neutral community model).

neutral_model()
Sloan's Neutral Community Model
plot(<ecodive_neutral_model>)
Plot a Neutral Community Model Fit

Phylogenetic community structure

How closely related the taxa in each sample are along a phylogeny (mean pairwise and nearest taxon distances), and whether more or less than in random communities (NRI and NTI). See also Faith’s PD, faith().

mpd() weighted_mpd() mntd() weighted_mntd()
Mean Pairwise and Mean Nearest Taxon Distance
mpd_ses() mntd_ses() plot(<ecodive_mpd_ses>) plot(<ecodive_mntd_ses>)
Net Relatedness and Nearest Taxon Indices (SES of MPD and MNTD)

Longitudinal

Repeated measures of the same subjects over time (q2-longitudinal). Each subject’s change from one time point to the next or from a baseline, a control chart of a variable over time, distances between subjects in how their features vary together (NMIT, then tested with permanova()), and the features that change most predictably over time (feature volatility, with random_forest()).

first_differences()
First Differences Within Subjects
first_distances()
First Distances Within Subjects
volatility()
Volatility of a Variable Over Time
nmit()
Nonparametric Microbial Interdependence Test (NMIT) Distances
plot(<ecodive_first_differences>) plot(<ecodive_first_distances>) plot(<ecodive_volatility>)
Plot Longitudinal Results
feature_volatility()
Feature Volatility
plot(<ecodive_feature_volatility>)
Plot a Feature Volatility Result

Batch Correction

Remove batch effects (study, sequencing run, extraction kit) from a table while keeping the effects of named covariates (MMUPHin, ComBat).

batch_mmuphin()
MMUPHin Batch Correction
batch_combat()
ComBat Batch Correction
plot(<ecodive_batch>)
Plot a batch correction

Prediction

Predict each sample’s class or a number from its features with a random forest (q2-sample-classifier’s workflow on scikit-learn’s trees), with cross-validated and out-of-bag accuracy, ROC curves and feature importances; or with a compositional lasso (penalized log-contrast regression, zeroSum’s and coda4microbiome’s), which picks out the features whose log ratio predicts the outcome.

random_forest()
Random forests
predict(<ecodive_random_forest>)
Predict with a random forest
plot(<ecodive_random_forest>)
Plot a random forest
coda_lasso() coda_lasso_pairwise()
Compositional lasso: penalized log-contrast regression
predict(<ecodive_coda_lasso>) predict(<ecodive_coda_lasso_pairwise>)
Predictions from a compositional lasso
plot(<ecodive_coda_lasso>) plot(<ecodive_coda_lasso_pairwise>)
Plot a compositional lasso

Supervised

Ordinations that look for the axes that separate known groups. They always find some, so validate them with a permutation test such as permanova().

lda()
Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)
capda()
Discriminant Canonical Analysis of Principal Coordinates (CAP)
plsda()
Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA)
oplsda()
Orthogonal Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (OPLS-DA)

Find and Browse Distance Tests

Spatial

Spatial structure among samples from their positions (coordinates, geographic distances or spatial weights). Moran’s I tests whether a variable is more alike at nearby sites; Moran’s eigenvector maps turn positions into spatial variables for constrained ordination and variation partitioning.

moran_i()
Moran's I Test of Spatial Autocorrelation
dbmem()
Distance-Based Moran's Eigenvector Maps
plot(<ecodive_dbmem>)
Plot Moran's eigenvector maps

Interpreting Differences

Which taxa drive the differences between groups.

simper()
Similarity Percentages (SIMPER)
